answer: The prism test I would run is Fishing boat skipper logbook with fisheries inspector stamp: each logbook is seasons of recorded catches checked by a fisheries inspector, so a farm must sail a hundred real boats, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the anchor of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head. The summit is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
